item.title: KING NOBUYOSHI GODWIN: 5 POINTS GALLERY FEATURED ARTIST — Fri Nov 27, 5:00 PM — 5 Points Gallery
item.description: 5 Points Gallery, an artist-owned contemporary art gallery in downtown Durham, is pleased to announce an exhibition of paintings by Featured Artist King Nobuyoshi Godwin, whose vibrant, imaginative work reflects his experience of autism and synesthesia. Bringing together expressive animals, vivid colors, and numbers that convey emotion, Godwin creates playful worlds filled with unexpected connections. In a painting inspired by the African shoebill, King transforms the imposing bird into a potential friend, welcoming it into his colorful world of unlikely companions. Throughout the gallery, visitors can also enjoy work by our Triangle-based artists, offering a refreshing mix of painting, sculpture, fused glass, mixed media, and finely crafted furniture, with each artist bringing a distinct creative perspective. item.title: Film Screening: The Daytrippers (1996) — Fri Nov 27, 7:30 PM — Shadowbox Studio
item.description:
Join us for the final film of our messy movie marathon! Eliza D’Amico thinks her marriage to Louis is going great until she finds a mysterious love note to her husband. Concerned, she goes to her mother for advice. Eliza, her parents, her sister Jo, and Jo’s boyfriend all pile into the station wagon and go to the city to confront Louis with the letter. On the way, the five explore their relations with each other and meet many interesting people.
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Intermediate Stained Glass: Experience Required — Sat Nov 28, 10:00 AM — Fusion Gallery
item.description:
This four hour class builds on the basics of the copper foil, or “Tiffany,” method of creating stained glass. This process includes cutting, grinding, foiling, and soldering individual glass pieces. Students will also learn to work with tinned copper wire to create fine details and flourishes. All materials are included in class pricing.
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Downtown Durham Historian-Guided Tour — Sat Nov 28, 2:00 PM — Lucky Strike Tower
item.description:
Experience the history of downtown Durham, strolling between the city’s historic sites. Learn of Durham’s pivotal role in the industrialization of the American South, how a Durham banking magnate transformed the lives of millions of rural farmers, the tobacco factories that powered the city’s future, and much more.
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Downtown Durham African American Historian-Guided Tour — Sat Nov 28, 4:00 PM — CCB Plaza
item.description:
Durham: the mecca of black capitalism and the center of North Carolina’s African American business community. Join a local historian on this guided walking tour of Durham’s Black Wall Street, hearing the stories of how a humble sharecropper became the owner of the largest black-ned company in American history, and seeing some of the sites related to their stories. Learn how businessmen, labor organizers, educated academics, and craftsmen each contributed to the unique history of Durham’s African American community.
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Partner Yoga: A Practice for Two — Sat Nov 28, 4:30 PM — Yoga Off East
item.description:
NOTE: Your registration covers TWO people (yourself + your guest). Only one person of the pair needs to register. In this workshop, we invite you to discover and explore what it takes to practice yoga asana with another person. Whether you come with a significant other, bestie, yoga buddy, or family member, practicing partner yoga is always a lot of fun. We open the practice by being together, breathing together, and creating connection. Then we practice many familiar yoga poses in partnership – doing some poses together and giving each other hands-on adjustments and assists in others. This practice is a safe place to laugh, build trust, and be curious. Often participants say that it teaches us about communication not only with our own bodies but with those of other people. Please join us after our studio session has concluded to enjoy a cup of tea! To get a glimpse into what partner yoga looks like check out our video https://youtu.be/pQIOxHE0sW8.
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: A Taste of Saved Messages — Sat Nov 28, 6:00 PM — NorthStar Church of the Arts
item.description:

The night opens with a welcome reception, followed by an elevated chef’s dinner by Chef Caleb of Taste of BLK. Then enjoy a first look at Saved Messages, a funny, heartfelt new play by Carlita Victoria about mental health, resilience and the voices that carry us through. Whether you’re a foodie, a theatre lover, or looking for a meaningful night out with friends and family this holiday weekend, there’s a seat for you. All are welcome! item.title: Durham Ghost Walk — Sat Nov 28, 8:00 PM — Fate & Folklore
item.description:
Explore the spooky side of Durham’s history on this tour of the city’s most haunted locations. From the disgraced sons of tobacco giants who continue to roam their old factories, to tales of tragic accidents whose victims still haunt the site of their end, and murder victims who stubbornly cling to their possessions, Durham, NC, has a shadowy side to its history. Travel through the city with the assistance of a professional historian guide, while hearing about the city’s creepiest folklore.
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Leader as Coach (2 days) — Wed Dec 2, 9:00 AM — None
item.description:
For employees of Duke University and DUHS Continuing Education Credits (CEUs): 0.6 Duration: Two days; 9:00 AM - 12:00 PM both days.
PRE-REQUISITE: Please note that you must have successfully completed Fundamentals of Coaching prior to attending this course. If you have not completed Fundamentals of Coaching, you can register by clicking Fundamentals of Coaching.
For employees to be engaged in their work, they must grow in both knowledge and skills. Managers want employees to strive toward higher levels of performance, but how do employees grow as leaders? What kind of coaching does an employee need from his or her manager? This workshop will address why developing leaders through a coaching relationship is so important. We will explore several coaching methods and the competencies they require. The session will provide opportunities for developing your leadership philosophy through coaching.
Source: Duke University

item.title: Maixner Pain Research Symposium 2026 — Wed Dec 2, 9:30 AM — None
item.description:
The 4th Annual Maixner Pain Research Symposium, in honor of the late Dr. William "Bill" Maixner, is co-hosted this year by the Comparative Pain Research and Education Center at NC State University and the Department of Anesthesiology at Duke University. This event brings together pain researchers and clinicians from North Carolina academic hubs, including Duke University, UNC-Chapel Hill, NC State University, and Wake Forest University, to 1) share exciting new advances in pain research and pain management, 2) stimulate organic collaborative opportunities, and 3) promote professional development of early career students and trainees.
Source: Duke University

item.title: AI for Research (AIR) – Introduction to AI Tools in Qualitative Software — Wed Feb 24, 10:00 AM
item.description:
Discover how artificial intelligence can streamline workflows, uncover hidden patterns, and empower breakthroughs in your field. Learn practical applications of AI through Odum Institute AIR series that can revolutionize your research process.
This course will introduce participants to generative AI tools in qualitative software—ATLAS.ti, MAXQDA, and NVivo. These tools can be used to summarize textual documents through AI-assisted memo writing and to support coding, with each program taking a different approach to integrating human judgment and AI features.
The course will also demonstrate how ChatGPT can be used to code textual data, how to create effective prompts, and how to import results from ChatGPT into qualitative software for further analysis. The course will be based on presentation and lecture but will provide brief exercises for hands-on exercises to be completed outside of the course.
Registration and fee (refundable upon attendance of course) are required for Zoom link

item.title: Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage — Wed Feb 24, 10:00 AM — Gregg Museum of Art & Design
item.description:
Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design presents a series of vignettes exploring spaces of dignity, belonging, safety, and imagination within Black communities across North Carolina. Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. Through stories of triumph and adversity, Community Stories honors the ways Black Americans have sustained and uplifted their communities through family, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, and soulful imagination, while inspiring future generations.
Source: NC Cultural Resources

item.title: You Are Here Exhibition — Wed Feb 24, 10:00 AM — Witherspoon Student Center
item.description:

The exhibition is a speculative, immersive world-building study that invites guests to explore (geo)locating self and home amid a rapidly and frequently changing post-pandemic “new” world. It will be on display in the art gallery at the African American Cultural Center from Oct. 28, 2026, to Feb. 28, 2027. A behind-the-scenes look at the exhibition is set for Nov. 11.
Source: NC State African American Cultural Center

item.title: Mecklenburg's Declaration: NC's Revolutionary Presbyterians — Thu Feb 25 — Presbyterian Heritage Center
item.description:
An article published in the April 30, 1819 edition of the Raleigh Register and North Carolina Gazette proclaimed the following: “It is not probably known to many of our readers, that the citizens of Mecklenburg County, in this State, made a Declaration of Independence more than a year before Congress made theirs. The following Document on the subject has lately come to the hands of the Editor from unquestionable authority, and is published that it may go down to posterity.”
The document in question was called the Mecklenburg Declaration of Independence, and it had allegedly declared Mecklenburg “free and independent” from British rule on May 20, 1775. Of the 27 men who were said to have signed the document, almost all were Presbyterian.
But many people were confused – why were they just now hearing about this revolutionary action? The original document burned in a house fire in 1800, and the published version had been reconstructed from notes made by the clerk of the 1775 meeting.

item.title: Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage — Tue Feb 23, 10:00 AM — Gregg Museum of Art & Design
item.description:
Community Stories: Sustaining North Carolina’s Black Heritage at the Gregg Museum of Art & Design presents a series of vignettes exploring spaces of dignity, belonging, safety, and imagination within Black communities across North Carolina. Featuring historical photographs, contemporary images, artworks from the Gregg Museum collection including a handmade guitar by Freeman Vines, and ephemera from community partners, the exhibition reflects on place, memory, creativity, and spiritual resilience across generations. Through stories of triumph and adversity, Community Stories honors the ways Black Americans have sustained and uplifted their communities through family, entrepreneurship, cultural expression, and soulful imagination, while inspiring future generations.
Source: NC Cultural Resources
